title: A left fold in f32
prompt: Write sum32(xs: list[float]) -> float for a non-empty list: start from the first element, add the rest left to right, and round to f32 after every add with the f32 helper the starter gives you. Python floats are 64-bit doubles, so nothing rounds to f32 unless you ask. Values print with %.9g, enough digits to tell f32 results apart.
hints: Two things are off: sum starts from 0 instead of the first element, and nothing rounds to f32. (Since Python 3.12, sum of floats even uses extra precision, which is the opposite of what you want here.)
Start with acc = xs[0], then for each y in xs[1:] set acc = f32(acc + y).
Starting from 0 breaks [-0.0] (since 0 + -0.0 is 0.0), and skipping the rounding breaks [16777216.0, 1.0, 1.0] (in f32 each + 1 rounds away).
explain: Rounding after every add is what f32 hardware does, and starting from the first element (not from 0) keeps -0.0 and matches the spec's fold exactly. 3e38 + 3e38 overflows to inf in f32 even though it fits in a double, so the next - 3e38 can't bring it back. The f32 helper catches the OverflowError that struct.pack raises there and returns infinity, which is what the hardware rounds to.
